practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution provides for the establishment of the Finance Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 280 of the Constitution of India provides that the President shall, within two years from the commencement of the Constitution and thereafter at the expiration of every fifth year or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary, constitute a Finance Commission. [Primary Reference: Article 280, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Who has the constitutional authority to constitute the Finance Commission in India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India under Article 280 of the Constitution. The Commission consists of a chairman and four other members appointed by the President. [Primary Reference: Article 280(1), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Who was the Chairman of the First Finance Commission of independent India?
practiceQuestions.sol: The First Finance Commission was constituted in 1951 under the chairmanship of K. C. Neogy. It submitted its report in 1952. [Primary Reference: Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951 / Union Budget Archives]

practiceQuestions.q: The qualifications of members of the Finance Commission and the manner in which they are selected are determined by:
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 280(2) of the Constitution mandates that Parliament may by law determine the qualifications which shall be requisite for appointment as members of the Commission and the manner in which they shall be selected. Pursuant to this, Parliament enacted the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951. [Primary Reference: Article 280(2), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Under whose chairmanship was the Fifteenth (15th) Finance Commission constituted?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 15th Finance Commission was constituted in November 2017 under the chairmanship of N. K. Singh to make recommendations for the period 2020-25 (and later extended to cover 2021-26). [Primary Reference: Ministry of Finance Notification / 15th Finance Commission Report]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following bodies submits its report directly to the President of India, who then causes it to be laid before each House of Parliament?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 281 of the Constitution, the President shall cause every recommendation made by the Finance Commission under the provisions of this Constitution together with an explanatory memorandum as to the action taken thereon to be laid before each House of Parliament. [Primary Reference: Article 281, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Grants-in-aid of the revenues of the states out of the Consolidated Fund of India are governed primarily by which constitutional article?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 275 of the Constitution provides for grants-in-aid of the revenues of such States as Parliament may determine to be in need of assistance, and different sums may be fixed for different States, based on the recommendations of the Finance Commission. [Primary Reference: Article 275, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: The Finance Commission is essentially which type of body under the Indian constitutional scheme?
practiceQuestions.sol: Since the Finance Commission is explicitly created by Article 280 of the Constitution of India, it is a constitutional body. [Primary Reference: Article 280, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following appoints the Chairman and members of the Finance Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 280(1) specifies that the Finance Commission shall consist of a Chairman and four other members to be appointed by the President. [Primary Reference: Article 280(1), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which amendment extended the scope of the Finance Commission to recommend measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of Panchayats and Municipalities?
practiceQuestions.sol: The 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts of 1992 added clauses (bb) and (c) to Article 280(3), mandating the Central Finance Commission to recommend measures to augment state consolidated funds to supplement resources of Panchayats and Municipalities, based on recommendations of State Finance Commissions. [Primary Reference: Articles 280(3)(bb) & 280(3)(c), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary constitutional nature of the recommendations made by the Finance Commission to the Union Government?
opts: Binding on the Union Government and enforceable by courts
Binding only if approved by a two-thirds majority in Parliament
Binding on both Union and State governments equally
practiceQuestions.sol: The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are purely advisory in nature and are not binding upon the Government of India. It is up to the Union government to implement them or not, though conventionally most recommendations regarding tax devolution are accepted. [Primary Reference: Supreme Court / Constitutional Precedents on Article 280]

practiceQuestions.q: How has the share of states in the divisible pool of central taxes evolved across recent Finance Commissions (from the 14th to the 15th Finance Commission)?
opts: Increased from 32% to 42%, and maintained at 41% (adjusting for Jammu & Kashmir bifurcation)
Shifted completely from tax devolution to discretionary grants
practiceQuestions.sol: The 14th Finance Commission drastically raised the states' share in the divisible pool of central taxes from 32% to 42%. The 15th Finance Commission recommended 41%, retaining the 42% share but adjusting 1% downwards specifically to account for the conversion of the erstwhile State of Jammu and Kashmir into two Union Territories. [Primary Reference: 14th and 15th Finance Commission Reports / Ministry of Finance]

practiceQuestions.q: Which parameter carried the highest weightage in the horizontal tax devolution formula recommended by the 15th Finance Commission?
practiceQuestions.sol: Income distance received the highest weightage of 45% in the 15th Finance Commission's horizontal devolution criteria. Income distance is the distance of a state's per capita GSDP from the state with the highest per capita GSDP, designed to promote equity by favoring lower-income states. [Primary Reference: Report of the 15th Finance Commission for 2021-26]

practiceQuestions.q: Why was the 'Demographic Performance' criterion introduced as a new parameter in tax devolution starting from the 15th Finance Commission?
opts: To penalize states with high population growth rates
To reward states that successfully undertook population control measures relative to states that lagged behind
To replace the income distance criterion completely
To allocate funds exclusively for elderly healthcare
practiceQuestions.sol: The 15th Finance Commission introduced the 'Demographic Performance' criterion (with a 12.5% weight) to reward states that have made progress in population control, using the 1971 population census as a base line, thus ensuring that states performing well on population control are not penalized for using the 2011 census for other metrics. [Primary Reference: 15th Finance Commission Report - Vol I]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the primary difference between 'Vertical Devolution' and 'Horizontal Devolution' in the context of the Finance Commission?
opts: Vertical involves sharing between Centre and States combined, while horizontal involves sharing between different Union Territories.
Vertical relates to the division of tax revenues between the Centre and the States, while horizontal relates to the distribution of that states' pooled share among individual states inter se.
Vertical is managed by NITI Aayog, whereas horizontal is managed by the Finance Commission.
Vertical deals with loans, while horizontal deals strictly with grants.
practiceQuestions.sol: Vertical devolution determines the aggregate share of all states combined out of the divisible pool of central taxes. Horizontal devolution determines how this aggregate share is distributed among the individual states based on equity and efficiency criteria. [Primary Reference: Economic Survey / Finance Commission Concepts]

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following items constitutes the 'divisible pool' of taxes for devolution to states?
opts: All taxes levied and collected by the Union, excluding cesses, surcharges, and specific central levies earmarked for specific purposes
Gross tax revenue of the Centre including all cesses and surcharges
Only corporation tax and personal income tax
Only GST collected by the Central Government
practiceQuestions.sol: The divisible pool consists of all central taxes and duties (except Central GST, cesses, and surcharges levied under specific articles, and specific service taxes if any), which are collectible by the Union and shareable with the states as per the recommendations of the Finance Commission. [Primary Reference: Article 270, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: What role does the Finance Commission play regarding fiscal federalism in India?
opts: It acts as a balancing wheel of Indian fiscal federalism by correcting vertical and horizontal fiscal imbalances.
It completely eliminates the financial autonomy of states to ensure unitary control.
It sets monetary policy interest rates for state cooperative banks.
It regulates foreign direct investment inflows into state public sectors.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Finance Commission is universally described as the 'balancing wheel of Indian fiscal federalism' because its statutory mandate is designed to bridge the structural fiscal gaps between revenue capacities and expenditure responsibilities of both the Centre and the states. [Primary Reference: Landmark Supreme Court Judgments / Indian Polity by M. Laxmikanth]

practiceQuestions.q: Why has the proliferation of cesses and surcharges by the Union Government become a point of contention in Centre-State financial relations?
opts: Because cesses and surcharges are shared equally with all foreign nations.
Because cesses and surcharges are excluded from the divisible pool, reducing the total tax revenue shared with states.
Because they are collected exclusively by State governments without Central oversight.
Because they are illegal under Article 265 of the Constitution.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 270, cesses and surcharges levied by the Centre are not part of the divisible pool of taxes shared with states. An increase in the proportion of gross tax revenue collected through cesses and surcharges shrinks the divisible pool, impacting the overall untied fund transfers to states. [Primary Reference: Article 270 & 271, Constitution of India / Economic Survey]

practiceQuestions.q: How do grants recommended by the Finance Commission differ from discretionary grants given under Article 282?
opts: Finance Commission grants are statutory and rule-based, whereas Article 282 grants are discretionary and given for public purposes.
Finance Commission grants are decided solely by the Prime Minister, whereas Article 282 grants are decided by the Supreme Court.
Finance Commission grants can only be used for defense, while Article 282 grants are for agriculture.
There is no constitutional or functional difference between them.
practiceQuestions.sol: Grants recommended under Finance Commission recommendations (Article 275) are institutionalized, rule-based transfers. Conversely, grants under Article 282 are discretionary grants (formerly channeled through the Planning Commission) given by the Union for public purposes outside the Finance Commission framework. [Primary Reference: Articles 275 & 282, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of including 'Forest and Ecology' as a criterion in the horizontal devolution formula by recent Finance Commissions?
opts: To compensate states for the opportunity costs arising from unutilized forest cover and restrictions on commercial timber felling.
To fund private wildlife sanctuaries owned by corporate entities.
To penalize states with high industrial pollution levels.
To force states to clear forests for infrastructure expansion.
practiceQuestions.sol: The 'Forest and Ecology' criterion was introduced to reward states for maintaining dense forests, which provides massive ecological benefits to the entire nation while imposing economic opportunity costs on those forested states due to developmental restrictions. [Primary Reference: 14th and 15th Finance Commission Reports]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Finance Commission of India:
1. It is a constitutional body established under Article 280 of the Constitution.
2. The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are binding on the Union government.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body set up under Article 280. Statement 2 is incorrect: Its recommendations are advisory in nature and not legally binding on the Union government. [Primary Reference: Article 280, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The First Finance Commission was set up in 1951 and was headed by K. C. Neogy.
2. The 15th Finance Commission was chaired by N. K. Singh.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The First Finance Commission was indeed constituted in 1951 under K. C. Neogy, and the 15th Finance Commission was constituted under the chairmanship of N. K. Singh. [Primary Reference: Finance Commission Act, 1951 / Union Budget Notifications]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the composition and qualifications of the Finance Commission:
1. The Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President.
2. The qualifications of members and the mode of their selection are specified directly and exhaustively in Article 280 itself.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Finance Commission comprises a Chairman and four members appointed by the President. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 280(2) empowers Parliament by law to determine the qualifications and selection manner; the Constitution does not list them exhaustively in Article 280 itself, leading to the enactment of the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951. [Primary Reference: Article 280(1) & (2), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the scope and functions of the Finance Commission:
1. It recommends the distribution between the Union and the States of the net proceeds of taxes which are to be, or may be, divided between them.
2. It recommends the principles which should govern the grants-in-aid of the revenues of the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct under Article 280(3)(a) and (b) of the Constitution, which outline the core statutory duties of the Finance Commission regarding vertical/horizontal tax devolution and Article 275 grants-in-aid. [Primary Reference: Article 280(3), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts and the Finance Commission:
1. They empowered the Central Finance Commission to suggest measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of local bodies.
2. They paved the way for the establishment of State Finance Commissions in every state.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The 73rd and 74th Amendments inserted provisions requiring State Finance Commissions (Articles 243I and 243Y) to review financial positions of Panchayats/Municipalities and amended Article 280(3) to link Central Finance Commission oversight based on those state-level findings. [Primary Reference: Articles 243I, 243Y, and 280(3), Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of the Finance Commission:
1. The Finance Commission has the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, while performing its functions.
2. It can summon witnesses, request the production of public records, and call for any information from any government office.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, the Commission possesses all the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including summoning witnesses and requisitioning any public record or document from any office. [Primary Reference: Section 8, Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 15th Finance Commission:
1. It recommended a horizontal tax devolution formula where 'Income Distance' was assigned the highest weightage.
2. It completely excluded demographic criteria from its horizontal devolution formula.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Income distance was given a 45% weightage, the highest among all criteria. Statement 2 is incorrect: The 15th Finance Commission explicitly introduced 'Demographic Performance' as a new criterion with a 12.5% weightage, alongside using the 2011 population data. [Primary Reference: Report of the 15th Finance Commission]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the distinction between the Finance Commission and NITI Aayog:
1. The Finance Commission is a constitutional body created under Article 280, whereas NITI Aayog is a non-constitutional, extra-constitutional executive body.
2. The Finance Commission makes binding allocations of plan grants, whereas NITI Aayog deals exclusively with statutory tax devolution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Finance Commission is constitutional (Article 280), while NITI Aayog is a cabinet-resolution-created executive body. Statement 2 is completely reversed: Finance Commission deals with statutory tax devolution and grants under Article 275, whereas it does not manage discretionary plan grants (which historically fell under the Planning Commission and now cooperative federalism platforms like NITI Aayog). [Primary Reference: Constitution of India & Cabinet Secretariat Resolutions]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'divisible pool' of central taxes:
1. All taxes and duties levied and collected by the Union are automatically part of the divisible pool.
2. Surcharges levied by the Union for specific purposes under Article 271 are excluded from the divisible pool.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect: Not all taxes are part of the divisible pool; cesses and surcharges are excluded under Article 270. Statement 2 is correct: Under Article 271, Parliament can at any time increase any of the duties or taxes referred to in articles 269 and 270 by surcharge, and the proceeds of any such surcharge form part of the Consolidated Fund of India exclusively for Union purposes and are excluded from the divisible pool. [Primary Reference: Articles 270 & 271, Constitution of India]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding State Finance Commissions in India:
1. They are constituted under Part IX and Part IX-A of the Constitution to review the financial position of Panchayats and Municipalities.
2. Their reports and recommendations are submitted to the respective State Governors, who cause them to be laid before the State Legislature along with an explanatory memorandum.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. State Finance Commissions are constituted quinquennially under Articles 243I and 243Y (inserted via the 73rd and 74th Amendments) to review local government finances, and their reports are laid before the respective State Legislatures by the Governor. [Primary Reference: Articles 243I & 243Y, Constitution of India]
